findings.reason: §2's own cost model describes a different program and its sole stated removal mechanism is a no-op on the program it bounds, so the 0.2 ms clause has nothing under it and a dispatched node would either miss the bound blind or re-derive the decomposition the plan was supposed to supply.
findings.text: §2 spends 107.8 ms, 61,330 launches, the two while-loops and the 29.4 ms of copies on "the present read" and then says "What removes it is tracking: in the steady state this read refines two points from the previous step's positions and rebuilds nothing" — but the read §2 is building and bounding is `support_read.read`, and that program is not the traced one and is not missing the mechanism §2 names. `solve-wall-breakdown` measures `nova.equilibrium.topology.read` (its own words: "The step's read stage runs nova.equilibrium.topology.read on the field"), a program that builds the contour tree; `support_read.read` instead calls `topology.read_at_stationary_points`, whose docstring states "No contour tree or null census is built: the supplied points are the census", and it already receives those points warm-started solved (`fixed_points.solve` from `seeds`/`previous` over the `maintain_rows` row window — §0 :58 says so itself). The only measurement of `support_read.read` in the cited prototype is "read (production read over a supplied jet field)", 141–144 ms per call, which that fragment calls "a floor above the sub-millisecond target independently of how the jets are built". So the 141–144 ms §2 must remove is nowhere decomposed, and "tracking" cannot be what removes it, because the present program already tracks and already builds no tree.

findings.reason: naming which cells carry the fit decides whether §2 clause (2)'s 0.2 ms is reachable at all, and the node is otherwise free to implement the 550-fit reading that cannot meet it.
findings.text: §2's first mechanism bullet says "It takes nodal flux derivatives from a cell-local quadratic fit over each hex cell's stencil … Each cell evaluates only its own fit, so no jets are averaged across cells", which puts the fit over every hex cell, while :87 says the read "evaluates the stencil fit only in the few cells that hold the tracked axis and X-point, never over every node". The two readings differ by roughly the cell count (about 550 fits against about two) and :87 prices the all-nodes version at the prototype's 0.51–0.72 ms, which is itself 2.5–3.6 times the 0.2 ms clause (2) allows.
